newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil trade stifled by volatile futures.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil trade stifled by volatile futures.

text.p: Volatile futures stifled physical trade on the NWE gas oil market on Tuesday, traders said.
With many European dealers absent on Monday, the market took time to digest Monday's $5.00 gains on IPE futures followed by an early slide on Tuesday.
"Nobody wants to stick their neck out until the screen has settled," said one trader.

Benchmark June IPE gas oil futures were trading $1.75 a tonne lower at $176 by 1119 GMT. Heating oil barges were still offered at June IPE +$3.50 for running refinery material at Rotterdam, and at +$2.00 fob Flushing.
First half June barges were talked weaker at June IPE +$1.00/+$2.00.
"End-user demand in Germany is below replacement level," said one trader.
Low sulphur diesel barges were offered slightly firmer at June IPE +$12, but buyers were seen relaxed.
